summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: "The Mystery of the Peacock's Eye" by Brian Flynn (1928, John Hamilton Ltd., London)

### Core characters
- **Anthony Lotherington Bathurst** ("Mr. Bathurst"): amateur detective, flat in London, Hotel Florizel letter, walks daily, "Mens sana" devotee, keeps "Encyclopædia of London," writes "Initial Summary of Facts."
- **Alexis, Crown Prince of Clorania** (alias "Mr. Lucius"; "Mr. X" at the Hunt Ball): to marry Princess Imogena of Natalia in December; blackmailed for £50,000; stays at Hotel Cassandra, Seabourne, suite 17; photo taken by Captain Willoughby at Seabourne last summer.
- **Chief-Inspector Richard "Dandy Dick" Bannister** (Scotland Yard, retiring): on holiday at Seabourne, horn-rimmed glasses; plural-precision speech ("data" as plural; "maxima").
- **Daphne Carruthers**: auburn-haired niece of late Major Desmond Carruthers (Chief Constable of Westhamptonshire, killed in motor accident March, a year earlier); lives 11 Lexham Gardens, Kensington; murder-victim mistaken identity.
- **Sheila Delaney**: only child of Colonel Daniel (Dan) Delaney (Westhampton Regiment; drowned 1917 at Nillebrook Water, Gallipoli leave); lives at "Rest Harrow," Tranfield; murdered at Seabourne; owned "The Peacock's Eye" emerald (~£20,000) left in Mutual Bank deposit.
- **Agnes "Pinkie" Kerr**: old nurse-companion, Devonian/Scots, ~60s; holiday at 4 Rolle Cottages, Otterton (Budleigh Salterton view postcard, July 3).
- **Alan Warburton**: nephew of Sir Felix Warburton (Mutual Bank frauds; arrested, suicide in cell); 19 Crossley Road, Westhampton; ex-lover of Sheila; blackmailer of Crown Prince; believed Crown Prince was Bannister.
- **Captain Willoughby**: Cassandra guest, fiancé of Lois Travers (Maida Vale, Crowborough Mansions); cousin Phipps-Holloway's racehorse "Sherlock Holmes"; paid notes to bookmaker Jacob Morley.
- **Sergeant Godfrey** (Seabourne County Police); **Sergeant Ross** (Tranfield); **Ronald Branston** (dentist, Coolwater Avenue corner, Lower Seabourne Road, Seabourne); **Mrs. Bertenshaw** (housekeeper); **Dr. Renfrew** (divisional surgeon); **Maynard** (Lauderdale Hotel manager), **John Martin** (reception clerk); **Jacob Morley** (Turf accountant, 9 Macbeth Court Mansions); **E. Kingsley Stark** (Mutual Bank Westhampton manager); **Churchill** (cashier); **Sir Matthew Fullgarney** (Lord Lieutenant; Dovaston Court; wife Pauline, Lady Fullgarney); **Lal Singh** (counterfeit Indian, really Herbert/no — the "Indian" ultimately Bannister in disguise); **Sir Austin Kemble** (Chief Commissioner; "Brigadier-General Sir Austin Mostyn Kemble"); **Cuypers** (Dutch police head, Amsterdam); **Stefanopoulos/Demetri** (Amsterdam fence, Jewish Quarter); **Falcon** (Grand Hotel, Westhampton proprietor); **Rogers and Davidson** (commercial travellers); **Macmorran** (new Chief-Inspector).

### Chronology
1. **Hunt Ball, Westhampton, February (last year)**: Major Carruthers (Chief Constable) with "Mr. X" (Bannister, incognito) meets Sheila; Alan Warburton present; Crown Prince present; Daphne dances with Crown Prince. Sir Felix suicide same day. Sheila dances with Mr. X; he refuses identity; "Au 'voir—Miss Sheila." Major drives Sheila home; Carruthers dies in March in motor accident.
2. **Letters to Crown Prince** (April 23 onward, Tranfield/Westhampton/London post-marks; five letters; £50,000 by 9th of next month; "Agony Column" of the Times). Bathurst takes case.
3. **July evening**: Bannister at Seabourne; Sergeant Godfrey calls him about Branston's surgery: Daphne (Sheila) poisoned with prussic/hydrocyanic acid from syringe in dentist's chair while Branston locked in work-room (brass bolt). Mrs. Bertenshaw released him.
4. Suit-case labelled "Daphne Carruthers, 11 Lexham Gardens," booked by phone at Lauderdale; John Martin identifies body.
5. Crown Prince's telegram summons Bathurst; "Daphne" phones from London alive; Sir Austin Kemble arranged.
6. Sheila identified by Daphne; Willoughby denies Miss Travers in mortuary.
7. Bathurst deduces passage swap, suit-case under car seat, car back at Rest Harrow; garage: Standard car; Seabourne Herald (July 5) in dashboard; postcard "X" with irides; visiting card of Alan Warburton with Branston's address on reverse; keys.
8. Lal Singh (Indian) visit ~month before murder claimed by Pinkie.
9. Stark reveals £100 cheque cashed; Peacock's Eye withdrawn from strong-room; ninety pounds in notes numbers.
10. Warburton confesses to Bannister: accuses Crown Prince; he is blackmailer; also Bannister's interview with Stark.
11. Stolen notes traced to Willoughby → from bookmaker Morley → from Branston → from Mrs. Bertenshaw (found £100 in art-pot in hall; repaid Branston £50).
12. Bathurst identifies Bannister as murderer; interviews Fullgarney (Lal Singh; Peacock's Eye history: Delaney/Carruthers/Fullgarney looted Sacred Peacock temple in Baluchistan near Bolan Pass; Lal Singh body-servant).
13. Amsterdam trip: Lal Singh (Bannister in disguise) arrested in Stefanopoulos's shop, Jewish quarter; beard pulled off. Cuypers, Stefanopoulos ("Demetri"); Sir Austin, Crown Prince aboard aeroplane/steamer SS Nicholas Maes out of Hull.
14. Trial: Bannister convicted; Bathurst reveals he whispered Fullgarney's name to Bannister (false lure); Lady Fullgarney's laugh.

Key trick: Bathurst's "wrong" whisper naming Sir Matthew Fullgarney.

## BOOK 2: "Dorothy at Skyrie" by Evelyn Raymond (1907, Platt & Peck Co.; illustrated)

### Core characters
- **Dorothy Chester** ("Dorothy C.", "Dolly"): adopted girl (~13, birthday April 2), brown eyes, curly brown hair; kidnapped earlier; now at Skyrie.
- **John Chester** ("father John"): ex-postman, lame (wooden feet, crutches; wheel-chair from post-office comrades).
- **Martha Chester** ("mother Martha", "Mrs. Chester"): housemistress, proud, jealous, sharp.
- **Jim Barlow**: tall lad, former truck-farm worker (Miranda/Mrs. Stott), from Baltimore; works at Deerhurst (Mrs. Calvert); loves Dorothy; "study" ambitions; kisses/grievances.
- **Mrs. Betty (Elisabeth Cecil Somerset-Calvert)**: old rich lady of Deerhurst; ~80; Great Danes Peter and Ponce; coachman Ephraim; wants to adopt Dorothy.
- **Seth Winters**: "Learned Blacksmith," justice of peace at up-mountain smithy; Mrs. Calvert's "Cousin"; organizes "Bee."
- **Alfaretta Babcock** (Alfy), **Baretta** (Retty), **Claretta** (Clary), **Diaretta** (Diary, baby): Cat Hollow; father "Pa Babcock" (Nanarchist, red hair, whiskers); mother Mrs. Babcock; brothers Matthew, Mark, Luke, John.
- **Archibald Montaigne**: nouveau-riche mill/money man; wife Mrs. Montaigne; daughter Helena (fourteen, blonde, delicate); son Herbert (horse Bucephalus; catboat Merry Chanter).
- **Peter Piper**: half-wit in red-feathered hat; Brindle the old cow.
- **Oliver Sands**: Quaker miller, Heartsease farm; loans $300 "payable on demand"; sold Hannah (écru cow) and calf.
- **Bill Barry**: auctioneer.
- **Jewel/Daisy-Jewel**: the calf; sold for $35 to Seth (bought by Mrs. Calvert).
- **Portia**: piebald calico pony, bought by Dorothy at auction for $35.
- **Lady Rosalind**: cat (Dorothy got stray kitten from Herbert).

### Events in order
1. Dorothy meets Babcock girls at stone wall; Alfy (big, bare-footed, freckled) jumps wall; they pick wild strawberries; Alfy reveals knowledge of Dorothy's history; Dorothy's birthday April 2.
2. Jim arrives with dogs Peter and Ponce; they escape (dog-chains). Jim knocks Mr. Montaigne down at Lower Riverside post-office; punches him; Justice Seth Winters.
3. Montaigne goes to justice; complaint withdrawn; Mrs. Calvert meets Montaigne family; Herbert and Dorothy talk (planked shad, water lilies).
4. Advertisement "Immediate. Pig. Cow. Horse. Skyrie." → traders arrive; Oliver Sands sells Hannah + calf (free to Dorothy).
5. Alfy knocks apart dog-churn; ghost sighting: Dorothy sees a figure (Peter) in garden at night.
6. Bee: neighbors repair farm; Mrs. Calvert's offer to adopt Dorothy refused.
7. Auction of Daisy-Jewel; Jim's board on Hannah's horns; Dorothy buys Portia.
8. Helena's picnic at south meadow ("Si Waterman's Folly" — mine shaft); snake bites Jim; Peter saves Herbert/Dorothy from falling; Seth cauterizes wound.
9. Montaigne proposes Europe trip; Dorothy declines.
10. Dorothy repays Oliver Sands with money from Seth (Baltimore law firm Kidder & Kidder; secret legacy fund); mine has iron/mineral spring; royalty deal.

Final line: "Well, Dorothy, good-by!"
